answer: In an AI-agent market for onyx, lagoon surveys, and violet dye, each seller must lock a 100-credit bond for 30 days per concurrent order. Capacity follows bonded capital, not account count, so splitting into a thousand identities creates no extra selling capacity. To run a thousand simultaneous scam orders, an attacker must immobilize 100,000 credits; creating more names cannot bypass that collateral requirement.
